question: What percent of young adults in the US move back in with their parents?
outcome: Share of U.S. 18- to 29-year-olds residing with at least one parent (co-residence, incl. COVID-era 'boomerang' moves), CPS monthly files.
citation: Fry, R., Passel, J. S., & Cohn, D. V. (September 4, 2020), 'A majority of young adults in the U.S. live with their parents for the first time since the Great Depression', Pew Research Center. Underlying data: U.S. Census Bureau Current Population Survey monthly files (IPUMS); historical series from decennial censuses 1900-1990 and CPS annual averages 2000-2019.

dataset.note: Lock5 3e ships no dataset for this question (checked lock5stat.com/datapage3e.html). Counts are documented reconstructions from the published percentages; provenance and denominator choices in CSV header comments.

conclusion: 52% of U.S. 18- to 29-year-olds (26.6 million of ~51.2 million) lived with a parent in July 2020, up from 47% in February 2020 (+2.6 million) and above the 1940 census record of 48% -- first majority since the Great Depression. Both nulls rejected (p < 1e-15). Men > women (55% vs 49%) and ages 18-24 far above ages 25-29 (71% vs 28%), all p < 1e-15.
